tool.name: Coding Potential Calculator 2
tool.description: Coding Potential Calculator 2 (CPC2): Predict coding potential of RNA transcripts
tool.command: #if $input.is_of_type('fasta.gz') gunzip -c '$input' > input.fasta && #else ln -s '$input' input.fasta && #end if CPC2.py -i input.fasta $orf $reverse -o 'cpc2_result' && mv 'cpc2_result.txt' '$output'

param.name: input
param.label: Input FASTA file
param.help: Nucleotide FASTA sequences to evaluate coding potential.

param.name: orf
param.label: Predict peptide sequence
param.help: If enabled, the peptide sequence and ORF start site will be included in output.

param.name: reverse
param.label: Check reverse strand
param.help: If enabled, the reverse complement strand will also be considered for prediction.

tool.help:
**What it does**
CPC2 (Coding Potential Calculator 2) is a fast, alignment-free tool that predicts whether an RNA transcript is protein-coding or non-coding, based on four sequence intrinsic features: ORF length, ORF integrity, Fickett score, and isoelectric point (pI) of the putative peptide. Unlike its predecessor CPC, it does not rely on sequence similarity search against a reference protein database, making it much faster while retaining high accuracy.
**Input**
A FASTA file of nucleotide (RNA/DNA) sequences.
**Output**
A tab-delimited file with one row per input sequence and the following columns:
1. Sequence ID 2. Transcript length 3. Peptide length (length of the longest ORF, in amino acids) 4. Fickett score 5. Isoelectric point (pI) 6. ORF integrity 7. ORF start position 8. Coding probability 9. Label (coding or noncoding)
